summary: Iter14 validates that escorts now surface in the On Campus and Exited (Checked Out) Presence columns in addition to Stepped Out, and that EscortsStrip filters out exited escorts. Backend: 10/10 new iter14 tests in /app/backend/tests/test_review_iter14.py pass in 5.17s — they validate (1) every escorts_present row carries a status discriminator ∈ {on_campus, temp_out, exited} plus a check_out_at field, (2) status derivation is correct (exited > temp_out > on_campus precedence), (3) checkout no longer removes the row but flips status to exited and populates check_out_at, (4) returning from step-out flips status back to on_campus, (5) historical /presence still returns escorts_present=[], (6) member rows still carry the ETA triple, (7) no duplicate escort_ids, (8) no heavy selfie payload leaks. iter11 regression also passes (5/5) since test_checkout_marks_exited_in_escorts_present was already updated by the dev. iter12+iter13 regression: 12/12 green. Total: 30/30 backend tests pass. Frontend (Playwright via JWT-injected admin session on /presence with seeded data: 1 on_campus 'Test Escort', 1 temp_out 'Raju Saheb' RED 391m late, 1 exited 'agape test'): VERIFIED — On Campus column renders column-escorts-on_campus sub-section with 1 row ('Test Escort · since 12:10 AM'), Es 1 chip, column-count-on_campus=2 (1 member + 1 escort). Stepped Out column unchanged (regression-safe): renders Raju Saheb row with RED 'Due 12:37 · 391m late' pill. EscortsStrip correctly filters exited rows — shows only 2 escorts (Test Escort + Raju Saheb), strip-count-escorts=2, the exited 'agape test' is NOT in the strip. On Tour / On Leave / Absent columns have NO escort sub-section and NO 'Es' breakdown chip. BUG FOUND on Exited column.

ui_bugs.component: Column.jsx — EscortRowsSection for the Exited column
ui_bugs.issue: The Exited (Checked Out) column does NOT render the column-escorts-exited sub-section nor any column-escort-row-* rows, even though (a) the column-count-exited badge correctly includes the escort (5 members + 1 escort = 6), (b) the column-breakdown-exited-escort chip correctly shows 'Es 1', and (c) the backend correctly returns the exited escort row with status='exited'. The escort sub-section is fully suppressed inside the displayList code path in Column.jsx.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/src/components/presence/Column.jsx — when `displayList` is truthy (paired column path used by On Campus + Exited), the JSX renders only displayList MemberCards and never reaches the `<EscortRowsSection escorts={escortList} columnKey={col.key} />` fallback. Move/duplicate the EscortRowsSection so it ALSO renders after the displayList map for paired columns. A one-liner: append `{escortList.length > 0 && <EscortRowsSection escorts={escortList} accent={col.accent} columnKey={col.key} />}` inside the `displayList ? (…)` branch (after the map but before the closing fragment), OR refactor to always render EscortRowsSection at the bottom irrespective of branch.

Optional sanity: verify pairedDisplay alignment vs PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS — constants.js declares PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS = {on_campus, exited} (comment says 'On Campus & Checked Out share a single sorted union') but Presence.jsx builds pairedDisplay from [...byColumn.temp_out, ...byColumn.exited] keyed as {temp_out, exited}. So PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS.has('on_campus') is true but pairedDisplay['on_campus'] is undefined → displayList resolves to null → On Campus accidentally falls through to the non-paired branch and renders the EscortRowsSection. That's why On Campus works today but Exited doesn't. This mismatch should be reconciled — either (a) PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS = {temp_out, exited} to match the union, or (b) pairedDisplay keys match the constant set ({on_campus, exited}).
critical_code_review_comments: Column.jsx lines 76-119 — the rendering branches do not compose: the displayList path silently drops escorts. Best fix is to lift `{escortList.length > 0 && <EscortRowsSection .../>}` out of the conditional and render it AFTER the column body regardless of which branch produced the member rows. This keeps the strip + columns consistent across paired/non-paired columns.

Presence.jsx line 215-222 — pairedDisplay only buckets temp_out + exited; the comment in constants.js line 15-17 explicitly says 'On Campus & Checked Out share a single sorted union'. The implementation pairs the WRONG two columns (Stepped Out + Checked Out). This is a separate latent bug: on the Presence Board, Stepped Out is currently sorted to match Checked Out instead of On Campus being sorted to match Checked Out. Recommend aligning to the stated intent.

server.py line 3046-3057 — status derivation is clean and the precedence (exited > temp_out > on_campus) is correctly enforced. Note: a checked-out escort with an unclosed open_excursion would currently still set status='exited' AND temp_out=False (good), but `expected_return_iso`/`overdue_minutes` will still be computed off the unclosed excursion. The frontend's `ExpectedReturnPill` is hidden on exited rows (the EscortRowsSection conditional doesn't show the pill for exited), so this isn't user-visible — but logically the server could null these fields on exited rows to keep the contract crisp.

test_review_iter11.py line 128-151 — the renamed test is correctly asserting both status='exited' AND check_out_at != null, plus the intermediate status='on_campus' before checkout. Good defensive coverage.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% — On Campus column, Stepped Out column, EscortsStrip-filtering, breakdown chips, and column counts all verified. Exited column escort sub-section MISSING (1 HIGH bug).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter14 backend is rock-solid (30/30 tests). The single open issue is FRONTEND ONLY: /app/frontend/src/components/presence/Column.jsx — the EscortRowsSection JSX block (lines 114-116) only renders inside the `else` branch (non-paired columns). When Column receives a truthy `displayList` (the case for the Exited column via PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS), the displayList branch never renders any escort sub-section. Verifiable by inspecting [data-testid="presence-column-exited"] — 0 nodes for column-escorts-exited and 0 column-escort-row-*. The count badge and 'Es N' chip correctly account for escorts, only the visual rows section is missing. A minimal fix is to add `{escortList.length > 0 && <EscortRowsSection escorts={escortList} accent={col.accent} columnKey={col.key} />}` inside the displayList branch after the .map(). Verify by reloading /presence and confirming the agape test escort row appears under an 'Escorts' sub-header in the Checked Out column with text 'In HH:MM → Out HH:MM' (both timestamps shown). Also reconcile the PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS vs pairedDisplay key-set mismatch noted in critical_code_review_comments[1].
rca of the issue: Root cause: Column.jsx conditional rendering structure (lines 76-119) splits into two mutually-exclusive branches based on truthiness of `displayList`. The EscortRowsSection block (lines 114-116) lives ONLY inside the `else` (non-paired) branch. The Exited column receives a non-null `displayList` from pairedDisplay[col.key] in Presence.jsx because PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS contains 'exited', so it never reaches the branch that renders EscortRowsSection. On Campus accidentally works because, despite being in PAIRED_COLUMN_KEYS, pairedDisplay only has temp_out + exited keys (Presence.jsx line 215-222), so pairedDisplay['on_campus'] === undefined → displayList resolves null → fallback branch is taken → EscortRowsSection renders. Reproduction: load /presence as admin with at least one escort with status='exited' for today (e.g. the persisted 'agape test' row). Observe Checked Out column header shows 'Es 1' chip and total count includes the escort, but no escort row is rendered inside the column body. Mitigation: render EscortRowsSection in both branches OR hoist it outside the conditional (preferred — single source of truth).
